facts.statement: Naturalist Louis Agassiz named the genus Helodus in 1838 based on isolated bead-like teeth from the late Paleozoic.
facts.quote: The genus Helodus was named by naturalist Louis Agassiz in 1838 to refer to isolated bead-like teeth from the late Paleozoic.

facts.statement: James William Davis described a fossil skeleton of Helodus simplex in 1890, which is now housed at the Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery.
facts.quote: A fossil preserving the scales and cartilaginous skeleton of H. simplex, which is housed at the Hunterian Museum and Art Gallery, was described in 1890 by James William Davis.

facts.statement: The first described skeleton of Helodus simplex was found in an ironstone mine in Staffordshire, England.
facts.quote: This specimen originated from Staffordshire, England and was found in an ironstone mine.

facts.statement: Fossils of Helodus date from the Late Devonian to the Early Permian periods.
facts.quote: with fossils belonging to the genus identified from the Late Devonian to the Early Permian periods.

facts.statement: The complete skeleton of Helodus simplex is known from multiple articulated specimens.
facts.quote: the skeleton of the species is completely known.

facts.statement: The endoskeleton of Helodus was composed of cartilage.
facts.quote: The endoskeleton of Helodus was made up of cartilage.

facts.statement: The first dorsal fin of Helodus featured a short, smooth fin spine supported by the synarcual.
facts.quote: The first dorsal fin had a short, smooth fin spine emerging from it, which was supported by the synarcual.

facts.statement: The fin spine on the first dorsal fin of Helodus was made of osteodentin.
facts.quote: This spine was made up of osteodentin.

facts.statement: Helodus is the sole member of the family Helodontidae and the order Helodontiformes.
facts.quote: The genus is the sole member of the family Helodontidae and the order Helodontiformes.

facts.statement: Helodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes and the subclass Holocephali, which includes living chimaeras.
facts.quote: It is a member of the class Chondrichthyes and the subclass Holocephali, which also includes living chimaeras.

facts.statement: Over 70 species have been attributed to Helodus based on similar teeth, but these likely belong to many different unrelated fish groups, making the genus a 'wastebasket taxon'.
facts.quote: Over 70 species have been attributed to this genus based on these indistinct bead-like teeth, which likely belong to many different unrelated groups of fish in the subclass Holocephali.

facts.statement: Researchers have tentatively suggested a relationship between Helodus and the order Eugeneodontiformes based on tooth similarities, but this requires further confirmation.
facts.quote: Michael Coates and coauthors have tentatively suggested that the genus may be related to the order Eugeneodontiformes due to similarities in their teeth, although they cautioned that further studies are needed to confirm this.

facts.statement: Helodus simplex lived in a shallow freshwater environment.
facts.quote: The ironstones that preserve Helodus simplex were formed in a shallow freshwater environment.

facts.statement: The time range for Helodus is from the Tournaisian to the Changhsingian, approximately 358.86 to 251.902 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tournaisian to Changhsingian (358.86 to 251.902 million years ago)
